definition: The energy transferred from other forms to electrical energy per unit charge by a source such as a cell, measured in volts; despite its name it is not a force, and for a real cell it equals the pd across the terminals only when no current flows.
A property of matter, positive or negative, that makes particles exert electric forces on each other; it is measured in coulombs (C), and an electron carries $-1.60 \times 10^{-19}\ \text{C}$.
A charged particle that is free to move through a material and so carries a current, such as a free electron in a metal or an ion in a solution.
The rate of flow of charge past a point, $I = \frac{\Delta q}{\Delta t}$, measured in amperes, where $1\ \text{A} = 1\ \text{C s}^{-1}$.

The work done per unit charge on a positive charge as it moves from one point in a circuit to another, following the current, $V = \frac{W}{q}$, measured in volts, where $1\ \text{V} = 1\ \text{J C}^{-1}$.
